# How to Turn Scanned Documents into Searchable Files with AI

You’ve probably got a shoebox of old photos, a stack of handwritten notes, or a folder of printed forms sitting in the cupboard. What if you could search inside them the same way you search your emails? With a free AI tool and a phone camera, you can turn those paper piles into searchable, text-ready files in minutes.

## Start with a photo or scan

Grab your phone and open the camera app. Hold it steady over the page you want to digitise—whether it’s a school assignment, a handwritten letter, or a printed invoice. Make sure the lighting is even so the text is clear. Snap the photo.

If you have a physical scanner, use that instead. Save the scan as a PDF or JPEG file on your computer or phone.

## Use an AI tool to extract the text

Now, open your browser and go to a free AI website like [Claude](https://claude.ai) or [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com). These tools can read text from images and turn it into editable text.

- In the chat box, type:
  *“Extract all the text from this image and return it as plain text.”*
- Then, upload your photo or PDF file.

The AI will read the text and show it back to you in a few seconds. You can now copy that text, paste it into a document, or search for keywords inside it.

## Fix any mistakes

Sometimes the AI gets a word wrong—especially with handwriting or faded print. Just scroll through the text and correct any errors. It’s much faster than typing everything yourself.

## Save your new searchable file

Once the text is clean, save it as a Word document, Google Doc, or even a plain text file. Name it something useful like “Year 10 History Notes 2023” or “Tax Receipt 2024”. Now you can search inside it anytime—just like an email.

## Bonus: Turn photos into searchable albums

If you’ve got old photos with names or dates written on the back, take a photo of each one and run it through the same AI tool. The AI will read the text, and you can save each photo with its description. Later, you can search for “Grandma’s birthday 1985” and find the right photo instantly.

---

## What this means for you

- **If you’re at home**: Digitise your kids’ artwork, old school reports, or family recipes so they’re never lost again.
- **If you’re studying**: Turn handwritten lecture notes into searchable text so you can find key points fast during exams.
- **If you’re just getting started**: Try it with one photo today—open your camera, snap a page, and paste the text into a Google Doc.

You don’t need fancy software or a degree in tech. Just a phone, a free AI tool, and a few minutes.
